Deputy Prime Minister Vitaly Neagu, formerly head of the customs service, then interior minister, and previously a lawyer at Sheriff Holding, is the overwhelming favorite in a race with no meaningful competition.



Turnout has fallen from 62 percent in 2016 to a record-low 26 percent in the 2025 parliamentary vote, weakening the legitimacy of a president whose term will run past the 2030 date when Transnistria’s separate fiscal space is scheduled to disappear.








Transnistria opened its presidential campaign on September 14. Candidates may be nominated until November 12 and must gather signatures from at least 2 percent of registered voters, about 8,000 people.
